Where it began

Kane Williamson was born in Tauranga, on the Bay of Plenty coast of the North Island, on 8 August 1990. He was playing senior representative cricket at 14, and he made his first-class debut for Northern Districts in December 2007, aged 17, as a pupil at Tauranga Boys' College, where he finished as head boy. He is said to have made 40 hundreds before he left school.

In 2008 he captained New Zealand at the Under-19 World Cup in Malaysia and took them to the semi-finals. Cricket ran a little further through the family too: his cousin Dane Cleaver went on to play for New Zealand.

The player

His first Test came against India at Ahmedabad in November 2010, and he marked it with 131, becoming only the eighth New Zealander to make a hundred on Test debut. In 110 Tests between 2010 and 2026 he scored 9,515 runs at 54.06, with 33 hundreds and a best of 251 against West Indies in 2020. By October 2026 he ranked 16th among all Test cricketers for runs and 12th for hundreds, and when he retired in June 2026 no New Zealander had made more Test runs.

He took over the captaincy in all formats in 2016 and led New Zealand in 40 Tests, winning 22 and losing only 10. The peak came in June 2021, when his side beat India by eight wickets to win the first World Test Championship final. Two years earlier he had been named Player of the Tournament at the 2019 World Cup, with 578 runs as captain.

What made him special

Through the 2010s Williamson came to be counted among the very best batters in the world. For years he was New Zealand's most productive number three since Stephen Fleming, and with Ross Taylor he formed one of the strongest top-order pairings his country has had. By August 2016 he had made a Test hundred against every other Test nation, and he was the youngest man to manage it. At the end of 2020 he rose to the top of the world Test batting rankings.

His off-spin was a more modest business. It brought him 30 Test wickets at 40.23 each, a gentle reminder that batting was the day job.

Away from the middle

He won the County Championship with Yorkshire in 2014 and the Indian Premier League with Sunrisers Hyderabad in 2016. Wisden named him a Cricketer of the Year, and in 2018 the ICC gave him its Spirit of Cricket award. When the ICC chose its Test side of the decade for 2011 to 2020, he was the one New Zealander in it. In 2014 he gave his match fees from a five-match one-day series against Pakistan to help those affected by the school attack in Peshawar.

And finally

He bats and bowls right-handed but writes with his left hand, so his autograph was perhaps the one thing he did the other way round. He ended his Test career 485 runs short of 10,000, which may be the only target he ever left for somebody else.
